articles.title: Swindon 2-1 Rotherham
articles.summary: Swindon 2-1 Rotherham
articles.body:
Joe Hungbo's brilliant free-kick sealed Swindon's 2-1 win over nine-man Rotherham.

United's Jili Buyabu was sent off after just four minutes for elbowing Jack Thomson.

Matty Virtue should have netted after Tom Nichols slotted him through, but his tame shot was saved by Julian Eyestone.

Virtue then dragged a low shot wide from distance before Mitch Clark nodded wide at the back stick.

Eyestone then did well to parry a Joe Snowden piledriver from outside the box.

Town went ahead on the stroke of half-time after Thomson's low rocket from 30 yards took a deflection, which wrong-footed Eyestone.

In the 79th minute, Dominic Iorfa was dismissed for a last-man foul on Virtue and from the free-kick, Hungbo bent superbly into the top corner.

United boss Alex Bruce was then sent off for his protests.

A clanger by Connor Ripley gave Rotheram hope after he dropped up a routine cross and Denzel Hall fired home in the 87th minute.

In added time, Sonny Aljofree spurned a simple chance to level against all the odds.

articles.title: Man City 0-1 Brighton: Yasin Ayari and Bart Verbruggen the heroes in historic win for Seagulls at Etihad
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Brighton inflicted Man City's second Premier League loss in the space of a week; Yasin Ayari netted the winner in the first half; the Seagulls are third in the table, within two points of both City and Arsenal
articles.body:
The result comes a week on from defeat at Aston Villa. City had previously not suffered consecutive league beatings since August 2025.

Brighton, dumped out of the Carabao Cup on penalties on this ground just four days ago, were excellent value in the first half, Yasin Ayari scoring what turned out to be the winner after Matheus Nunes made a mess of his attempted clearance.

But they also had to weather a City onslaught in the second period, matching style with steel and resilience. Maresca's side threw everything forward in search of a breakthrough, with Iliman Ndiaye rattling the crossbar, Erling Haaland going close from a corner and Nunes drawing an athletic save from a busy Bart Verbruggen.

The goalkeeper proved immovable, making seven saves in total.

Maresca had his hands on his head again when Nico O'Reilly's header flashed wide late on, as City contrived to squander chance after chance, out-creating their visitors overall but unable to make anything stick.

Jack Hinshelwood could have sealed it at the opposite end before Brighton's points were eventually confirmed, the first time they have triumphed at the Etihad.

With a club record points total at this stage of a top-flight campaign, Fabian Hurzeler's side look every bit like title contenders, adding another statement victory to their list of achievements after also seeing off Arsenal last month.

Brighton's players milked their celebrations with the away end. They deserved to. This rise warrants applause - and attention.

Are they in the title race? It's perhaps too early to tell, but by my estimation Fabian Hurzeler has a team with superb harmony, who play with complete tactical clarity. That greatly enhances their chances of doing something special.

Enzo Maresca professed to know exactly what Brighton were going to offer up, having hosted them just four days ago, but he could not devise a plan to stop their flow. City were outbattled in midfield and outrun overall.

If this was a tangible test of Brighton's stomach for the race, they passed with flying colours.

11: GOAL! Man City are cut open as Ayari benefits from Nunes' mistake to steer beyond Donnarumma.

22: HUGE CHANCE! Anderson stands up a lovely ball into the six-yard box but Ndiaye glances his header wide.

34: CHANCE! Donnarumma denies Gomez from a tight angle as Brighton push for a second.

48: MISS! De Cuyper wastes a huge chance to double Brighton's lead after slamming over the bar from Gomez's cross.

52: WOODWORK! Ndiaye rattles the crossbar with a fierce strike.

62: SAVE! Verbruggen saves from Nunes as waves of City pressure increase.

88: CHANCE! Rutter leads a one-man counter-attack and feeds Hinshelwood but the substitute dinks wide.

89: CHANCE! O'Reilly miscues his header as City's missed chances continue to mount.

90+4: SAVE! Doku skips past his man and is again denied by a wonderful performance from Verbruggen.

"We created enough to get some points but we didn't score. We did enough to deserve something. In this moment we need to move on.

"Sometimes [mistakes] happen. Unfortunately it's happening for our players. We need to analyse and understand what we can do better. We are conceding silly goals; we can avoid that.

"For sure, we are not happy. No one is happy when we lose a game. We were aware we weren't going to win all the games, these moments arrive, so we have to move on as quickly as possible."

"We expected a game where we had to suffer, facing one of the best teams in the world.

"We had to stick together and we had this feeling that defence wins today. Defence wins you tight games. We had a defensive mindset.

"We faced a lot of adversity during the game and really proud of how my players kept a clean sheet with quality and a bit of luck."

articles.title: Motherwell 1-0 St Mirren: Lukas Fadinger scores from the spot to end Motherwell's seven-match winless run
articles.summary: Report as Lukas Fadinger's penalty ends Motherwell's seven-match winless run; narrow defeat leaves St Mirren eighth, one place above their hosts
articles.body:
A host of chances were passed up by Alfred Johansson's men during a dominant display, which would have brought greater reward had they discovered a clinical touch in front of goal before the spot-kick as they moved into ninth spot on the table.

Saints dropped down to eighth as Craig McLeish's side, whose recent poor run of form continues.

The Lanarkshire side should have been ahead in the 10th minute when Tawanda Maswanhise was allowed time and space to fire in a shot from 18 yards, but he wildly blasted the effort high over the crossbar.

Another golden opportunity arrived moments later when a low cross from Emmanuel Longelo had Maswanhise racing towards the far post and the Zimbabwean was inches away from converting.

That sustained pressure on the Saints goal continued unabated in an impressive opening by Well, who forced a series of corners with the Buddies being swamped by waves of attacks.

Tom Sparrow then reacted first to a loose ball at the edge of the box and his shot was parried wide by visiting goalkeeper Jacob Chapman as the hosts piled on the pressure.

It may have been wasteful by the hosts, but the invention and creative spark down the flanks and from midfield was a much-needed return to the style which the Fir Park side had been serving up earlier in the campaign.

Ibrahim Said was next to miss a glaring chance when he steered a shot straight at Chapman when clean through in the 24th minute.

Saints had been let off the hook, but the Paisley side struggled to get themselves properly into the contest in a first half of little promise that they could breach the Motherwell goal as Joe Hodge went into the book for a lunge on Ryan Carr just before the break.

Martin Moormann rattled a volley inches over the top just seconds after the restart as the traffic continued to flow towards St Mirren's goal before Marcus Fraser saw yellow for a professional foul in the 52nd minute.

Another clear Motherwell miss came on the hour mark with Said swivelling inside the box and, from 16 yards, dragged the effort wide when he should have been busting the net.

St Mirren began building some pressure of their own in a bid to claim a smash-and-grab three points, but those hopes ended eight miutes from time as referee Don Robertson pointed to the spot after a VAR check for a Henry Fieldson handball.

Fadinger slammed home to secure a long-awaited for Motherwell and their under-pressure manager.

articles.title: Piratas informáticos atacan la web del Corinthians y anuncian el fichaje de Messi
articles.standfirst: En la noticia falsa ofrecían incluso detalles de una operación falsa
articles.summary: En la noticia falsa ofrecían incluso detalles de una operación falsa
articles.body: La página oficial en internet del club brasileño Corinthians fue blanco en la madrugada de este sábado de un ataque de piratas informáticos, que publicaron un extenso comunicado en el que anunciaron la supuesta contratación del argentino Lionel Messi como principal refuerzo del equipo para 2027. El falso comunicado de uno de los clubes más populares de Brasil detallaba la operación que supuestamente había permitido la contratación del astro argentino, actualmente en el Inter Miami estadounidense, e incluía declaraciones atribuidas al jugador en las que afirmaba estar feliz por la oportunidad de actuar en el fútbol brasileño. El anuncio, que sorprendió a algunos hinchas del club paulista, fue retirado poco después, cuando los responsables de la página detectaron la invasión y sustituyeron los contenidos por un aviso de que la plataforma estaba en mantenimiento. Los piratas informáticos llegaron a presentar una supuesta operación financiera para justificar la operación, que habría permitido al Corinthians incorporar al capitán de la selección argentina pese al elevado coste de su contratación. El club confirmó posteriormente que había sufrido un ataque cibernético dirigido contra su página oficial y aseguró que su equipo de tecnología de la información consiguió neutralizarlo rápidamente. En un comunicado, el Corinthians afirmó que no se habían constatado pérdidas financieras ni vulneración de datos o informaciones pertenecientes a la institución. Como medida preventiva, el equipo decidió reforzar los protocolos de seguridad de sus plataformas digitales y retirar temporalmente de servicio tanto su página oficial como la de su estadio, el Neo Química Arena, mientras realizaba las comprobaciones técnicas necesarias. El ataque se produjo pocas horas después de que el Corinthians derrotara por 2-0 al Mirassol en un partido correspondiente a la trigésima tercera jornada del Campeonato Brasileño. El resultado no impidió que el equipo, uno de los más populares de Brasil pero que enfrenta una grave crisis de resultados, se mantuviera entre los cuatro últimos en la clasificación de la Liga, que son castigados con el descenso. La invasión del portal del Corinthians se produjo pocos días después de que la página oficial de su histórico rival, el Palmeiras, también fuera objeto de un ataque informático. Los responsables de la invasión publicaron mensajes provocadores sobre la ausencia de un título mundial del equipo verdiblanco, uno de los principales protagonistas tanto del Campeonato Brasileño como de la Copa Libertadores en los últimos años

articles.title: Middlesbrough 3-0 Charlton Athletic: Will Lankshear scores twice in Boro win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Middlesbrough and Charlton Athletic at the Riverside Stadium on Saturday; Will Lankshear scores twice in a comfortable win for the league leaders.
articles.body:
Sebastian Berhalter opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Lankshear netted twice to take his tally to 15 in all competitions.

While the early exchanges were not without the odd nervy moment for a home side who came into the match unbeaten in their last 10 league matches, a long throw into the Boro box led to a quick counter and a shot from the division's top scorer Lankshear, resulting in a corner.

Charlton's Tyler Bindon picked up a yellow card inside 10 minutes for a late challenge and the resulting free-kick led to a header into the side-netting from Riley McGree, which seemed to give the home team and supporters a lift.

The first goal came shortly after, with the tricky feet of Amario Cozier-Duberry on the right ensuring he found enough space to pull the back to the edge of the 18-yard box for Berhalter, who produced a tidy finish to the goalkeeper's right. Arthur Okonkwo may well feel he could have done better, however.

Charlton went on to produce a couple of half-chances themselves, including a close-range shot from a wide angle from Joe Rankin-Costello, which was comfortably saved by Radek Vitek.

A deep cross from Cozier-Duberry then found the ever-dangerous Tommy Conway all on his own at the back post, but his curling shot went narrowly wide, while just after the half-hour mark a long Charlton throw was headed goalwards by Miles Leaburn and had Vitek scrambling, but missed the target.

McGree was given a deserved yellow for a heavy challenge on Charlton's Kayne Ramsay in the opposition box after losing control of the ball, with Ramsay having to be replaced at half-time.

The second goal came shortly before the break, with Berhalter producing a sumptuous through ball to find Lankshear. Cries of offside from the away side were ignored by the linesman and Lankshear produced a tidy dink finish to double the lead.

Charlton had a couple of threatening moments at the start of the second half, but Middlesbrough soon took control, with a McGree shot over the bar followed by a curling strike from Cozier-Duberry that looked destined for the top corner but went narrowly wide.

After a couple of dangerous looking crosses from Middlesbrough captain Callum Brittain that were begging to be converted, the victory was finally sealed in the 82nd minute.

Within seconds of being introduced from the bench, Charlton's Nathaniel Chalobah slipped on the edge of his own box and the ball dropped kindly to Lankshear, whose left-foot strike emphatically found the top corner, taking his league tally to 13 goals in as many games.

Lankshear was replaced immediately afterwards with what looked like cramp, with another excellent afternoon's work done and dusted.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Millwall 4-1 Derby County: Kyrell Lisbie scores twice in Lions win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Millwall and Derby County at The Den on Saturday; Kyrell Lisbie scores twice as the Lions romp past John Eustace’s struggling Rams.
articles.body:
The Lions roared out of the blocks as they scored three goals in the first 17 minutes to ensure what was just their second win in eight league games was secured with plenty to spare.

This was another worrying afternoon for the Rams, though, who were never in the contest and they remain second from bottom, four points from safety, and without a win in nine games.

Millwall were ahead after only three minutes when Camiel Neghli passed inside to Lyndon Dykes whose own ball found Lisbie in plenty of space and the winger placed his shot into the bottom corner via a slight deflection.

The lead was doubled in the 10th minute, though, when Neghli bent in an excellent cross from the left and Dykes' header across the six-yard box gave Lisbie the easiest of tap-ins.

Derby had a great chance to pull a goal back quickly, but their captain Carlton Morris skied his effort after being found at the back post by Rhian Brewster's low cross.

Instead, Millwall had their third with only 17 minutes on the clock when Neghli's ball over the top allowed Luke Cundle to run in behind a flat-footed defence and finish well past the helpless Jacob Widell Zetterstrom.

The Rams' goalkeeper could be forgiven what was going on in front of him, while the away supporters were singing "you're not fit to wear the shirt" at their own players.

Derby almost registered within a minute of the restart when Sam Szmodics fizzed the ball across the box and Morris' header was clawed behind by Millwall goalkeeper Max Crocombe.

The visitors were looking far more coherent - in contrast to their desperate start to proceedings - but were struggling to create clear-cut chances, with Brewster shooting at Crocombe from a narrow angle.

Cundle almost had his second of the afternoon for the Lions when his shot was beaten away by Zetterstrom before Caleb Taylor headed over for the hosts after Derek Mazou-Sacko's cross ricocheted into his path.

Mihaiolo Ivanovic then set up his fellow sub, Romain Esse, who should have added a fourth when his scuffed effort was kept out by Zetterstrom.

But extra gloss was added to the scoreline in the 84th minute when Alfie Doughty's mishit shot from distance ran for Ivanovic who unselfishly squared the ball for captain Jake Cooper to slam into the roof of the net.

Derby, at least, struck a consolation with three minutes left when Filip Bilbija fired in his first goal for the club after Crocombe had kept out a shot from Oscar Fraulo.

"I thought our start was excellent, to go 3-0 up after about 20 minutes, and I think you could probably see that part of it was some pent-up frustration from all of us.

"There have been certain games that we've played recently where we've probably not got what we deserved.

"But I've been involved in football long enough and if you lose and you don't get a sequence of results go your way, then everything you do is crap at that point, which is fine.

"So, we needed to show that we're capable of going and performing, and winning, and what was really pleasing today for me was I felt like we played the game with no fear.

"When you play with fear, you tend to just put it forward and play off second balls, but we played when it was on to play."

"Obviously, the first 20 minutes was really disappointing. The manner we conceded the goals was very soft.

"Obviously, we've got a lot of injuries at the back at the moment - seven defenders out - and it's only a makeshift defence, but we have to defend better if we want to get any results in games, and certainly in that first 20 minutes we didn't do it.

"Millwall started very quick and losing Joe Ward yesterday, just after training, was a blow as well.

"We had Max (Johnston) coming in and you've got to look at Jack Robinson - that was just his second appearance in the last four months and obviously he has had no pre-season.

"So, to come into an environment like this, at top Championship level, and expect him to perform at the level is always going to be tough.

"I was happy with the response after half-time; we battled and showed a good spirit."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Bolton Wanderers 2-3 Bristol City: Scott Twine scores stoppage-time winner for Robins
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bolton Wanderers and Bristol City at the Toughsheet Community Stadium on Saturday; Robins snatch late comeback victory as Scott Twine nets in added time.
articles.body:
The visitors trailed 2-1 with six minutes of normal time remaining but Sam Bell levelled before fellow substitute Twine ensured manager Skubala celebrated his 44th birthday with three points.

City's win was their first in five games while Wanderers have now gone three matches without victory and six weeks since their last success at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

Skubala's afternoon threatened to have an unhappy ending as Josh Sheehan and Sam Dalby put Bolton 2-1 up after Dom Ballard's fourth goal of the season fired the Robins into a 13th minute lead.

But Bell, a 78th minute replacement for Lorent Tolaj, tapped in Cam Pring's cross from close range before Twine converted from another substitute, Jed Wallace, three minutes into added time.

A section of the away fans had jeered Skubala's decision to take off Tolaj, who twice put the ball in the net only to be denied by an offside flag.

Trotters chief Steven Schumacher made eight changes from his team's previous 5-1 mauling by Middlesbrough while City were looking for a hat-trick of wins in the north west after successes at Preston and Burnley.

The treble was on when former Leyton Orient star Ballard tapped in Jason Knight's cross.

But the visitors led for just three minutes. There seemed little danger when Welsh international Sheehan, one of the three survivors from the Boro bashing, picked up possession. As defenders backed off Sheehan let fly from 25 yards, with goalkeeper Brad Collins well beaten.

That was the prelude to a chance-filled remaining half hour. Ballard teed up Tolaj, who forced a save from Jack Bonham - deputy for the injured Gavin Bazunu.

Tolaj should have done better and when he did find the net minutes later, his header was debatably ruled offside.

Collins denied Atsuki Ito before City fashioned a run of chances, none of which Luke McNally, Rio Cardines and Pring could convert.

However, Wanderers finished the half on the front foot and Ito struck Collins' right hand upright with a low shot and Sam Iling-Junior fired narrowly wide.

Tolaj's frustrating afternoon continued 10 minutes after the break. Played in by Ballard's pass, the Swiss striker clinically converted from 16 yards - only to be flagged offside again.

Bolton eventually hit the front after 57 minutes as Thierry Gale's cross was helped on by Ito and Dalby claimed the goal from close range.

Bonham came to Bolton's rescue, saving low down from McNally and then keeping out a low drive from Wallace.

Just as crucial was Collins stunning 83rd-minute save from Ruben Rodrigues. And instead of being 3-1 down City roared back to snatch victory.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: West Ham United 1-3 West Bromwich Albion: Hammers lose at home again as Baggies claim three points
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between West Ham United and West Bromwich Albion at the London Stadium on Saturday; Hammers make it back-to-back defeats at home as Baggies earn deserved win.
articles.body:
A second consecutive home defeat, in which his side have shipped six goals, contained few saving graces for Nuno, who faced the wrath of fans on the final whistle.

Albion, slick and measured, moved into the top four with their 3,000 travelling fans revelling in the discomfort of Nuno, once manager of Black Country arch-rivals Wolves.

The Hammers' bid to regain their Premier League status had already been undermined by patchy home form, notably the missed last-gasp penalties against Charlton and QPR which ultimately cost them three points and now the supporters' patience is wearing ominously thin.

After falling behind in nine of their previous 15 games, the Hammers' early anxiety was fuelled by Max Kilman's scything foul on Ousmane Diakite at the expense of a yellow card.

The home side fashioned the first major chance, Edvin Austbo's darting run setting up Mohammadou Kante, whose shot was deflected over the top by Jayson Molumby.

But after 20 minutes, West Ham were back in familiar territory, conceding first to a move of admirable simplicity.

Isaac Price's pass carved the Hammers' defence open and Jimmy-Jay Morgan's low centre was meat and drink for unmarked Norwegian midfielder Felix Horn Myhre from point-blank range.

Moments later, Price should have made it 2-0 but spooned wide from eight yards, and the mood was already turning toxic inside half an hour among the claret-and-blue factions until fortune played a kind hand.

West Ham skipper Jarrod Bowen's skimming low shot from an angle appeared to be covered by Albion goalkeeper Max O'Leary, but a telling deflection off Callum Styles smuggled it in off the near post.

Bowen's seventh goal of the season was not enough to placate disgruntled Iron fans, who booed the Hammers off at the interval and within three minutes of the restart Albion were back in front.

Myhre cushioned Price's left-wing cross into the path of Morgan, who was afforded the space to fire home his fourth goal of the season across home goalkeeper Mads Hermansen from the corner of the six-yard box.

Kilman's header from a Bowen corner and Kyle Walker-Peters' shot from distance were beaten out by O'Leary as the Baggies were finally made to weather some sustained pressure.

However within two minutes of Walker-Peters limping off with a thigh injury, and with Nuno using up all his five substitutes, Price's corner was only half-cleared to Styles, lurking 20 yards out, and his fierce, deflected shot gave the stranded Hermansen no chance.

West Ham went through the motions of a fightback but, apart from substitute Taty Castellanos' bicycle kick straight at O'Leary in added time, they rarely threatened to reduce the deficit.

"Many things went wrong - many, many things. It was a poor performance. The idea was to start well, but after West Bromwich scored it was very difficult.

"Then at the start of the second half, many fans were not even sitting down when we conceded a poor, poor goal."

Asked about visiting fans' taunts that he would be "sacked in the morning", he responded: "This is the reality: we can only change this if we win games. The solution is results, we have to go back to results.

"When you lose at home to Charlton, Southampton and West Brom, the only solution is to improve our game.

"There is pressure every day. We have conceded six goals at home in two games and we have to fix it. That cannot happen.

"In the first half we were too far away from each other and for the second goal we allowed too much time, with no cover in the box.

"The idea and the approach is to try and score first. That is the objective of any team and it's our responsibility to change it."

"That performance has been coming. I know how difficult this league is and some teams have spent heavily, but we have to have that belief that we can handle the pressure.

"In terms of that, and scoring at the right times, it was the complete performance.

"There was a bit of noise about West Ham conceding early, and how it might create a bit of pressure around them. I've watched them and they have been unlucky at times, with fine margins going against them, but I was so happy with the way we played."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Wolverhampton Wanderers 3-0 Cardiff City: Fer Lopez strikes in Wolves win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Cardiff City at Molineux on Saturday; Fer Lopez strikes as Wolves ease to victory over the Bluebirds.
articles.body:
Cesar Peixoto's side gave themselves the platform for victory by scoring twice in the first 15 minutes.

Wolves made it four games unbeaten and back-to-back wins without conceding, ending Cardiff's three-match unbeaten run.

The home side threatened first when a first-time low drive from Jordan James was tipped around the post by goalkeeper Nathan Trott.

Cardiff replied with a curling effort from Chris Willock that Jose Sa had to palm behind.

Wolves gained a 10th-minute lead when Lopez dived full-length to get his head to Hugo Bueno's clever chip over the defence, the ball bouncing before the Spaniard sent it beyond Trott into the net. It was Lopez's sixth Championship goal of the season.

Five minutes later it was 2-0 when the unmarked Armstrong exploited the freedom of the penalty area to head home Rafiki Said's cross.

Cardiff midfielder Jack Moylan fired straight at Sa after an awful pass out by Yerson Mosquera, who then slipped trying to atone for his error.

There was a two-minute delay just before the half-hour mark due to a medical issue in the crowd.

James went off injured in the 36th minute after twice receiving treatment to be replaced by Jean-Ricner Bellegarde.

Haiti international Bellegarde carved out the next chance but his cross just evaded the lunging Marshall Munetsi and Said.

Trott gifted Wolves the chance of a third goal when his pass to Will Fish was easily intercepted by Said, but the winger could only fire straight at the Cardiff goalkeeper.

Sa was called upon again in first-half added time to block Ollie Tanner's volley from Willock's cross.

Cardiff twice threatened again through Joel Colwill soon after the restart, but after arriving in dangerous positions, he fired straight at Sa on both occasions.

Wolves appeared to put the game beyond the visitors in the 58th minute, Ladislav Krejci rising to send a towering glancing header into the far corner of the net from Kieran Trippier's corner.

Any chance of a Cardiff comeback appeared to vanish when Sa smothered Alex Robertson's firm drive.

Wolves had three more chances to add to the scoreline but Bellegarde and substitute Rodrigo Gomes (twice) fired off target.

Cardiff briefly came more into the game in the latter stages.

Yousef Salech's header was fumbled against the post by Sa and Joel Colwill stabbed the rebound wide.

The visitors had the ball in the net in the 79th minute but Moylan was offside when he tapped home, after Sa saved Joel Colwill's shot from the edge of the box.

articles.title: Swansea City 4-0 Blackburn Rovers: Swans back to winning ways in thumping victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea City and Blackburn Rovers at the Swansea.com Stadium on Saturday; Swans back to winning ways with convincing victory for Vitor Matos’ side.
articles.body:
The hosts were three goals to the good by half-time thanks to Stephen Eustaquio, Joseph Opoku and Filip Lissah, with Scotland international striker Ross Stewart scoring his first goal for the Swans on the hour mark to complete the rout.

Tony Mowbray's Rovers side had arrived in Wales having won four of their previous six games, including last weekend's 2-0 home victory over Wrexham, but were simply blown away in the first half as Vitor Matos' men went on the rampage.

Looking to hit back from the 5-0 defeat at QPR last time out, Swansea's assault began as early as the fourth minute when Melker Widell put in a low cross from the right that Rovers managed to scramble away.

However, it did not take them long to open their account and once again the chance came from a raid down their right flank. This time Opoku led the charge, and his cross went along the six-yard box to find Eustaquio waiting at the far post for a simple tap-in.

The frustration was starting to build in the Rovers ranks and after Eom Ji-sung fired a free-kick from just outside the box inches wide, Moussa Baradjil picked up a yellow card for a lunging tackle on Widell.

Rovers' only shot of the first half came in the 26th minute when skipper Todd Cantwell blasted high over the bar after beating the offside trap.

Swansea's second goal arrived in the 32nd minute when Opoku ran on to a through ball from the centre circle by Stephen Welsh. Tom Atcheson could not control the ball and after it ran off his shin, Opoku simply stroked a shot past Balazs Toth in the Rovers goal.

Five minutes later it was 3-0 as the home side maintained their intensity and drive. At times their passing was irresistible and Lissah got his first goal for the club after taking down a long pass, controlling it in the box and then firing home.

Stewart should have made it 4-0 on the stroke of half-time but just failed to get a touch to a cross along the six-yard line with the goal begging.

Mowbray brought Augustus Kargbo and Hayden Carter on for the start of the second half and after Toth had snuffed out a double strike from Eustaquio and Widell, the visitors actually enjoyed some possession and territory.

They picked up a free-kick and a corner, but still Swansea keeper Lawrence Vigouroux was not called on to make a save.

A fourth goal then followed in the 59th minute as Stewart raced on to a flick by Eom before blasting the ball into the roof of the net with his left foot to open his Swansea account.

articles.title: El fondo volvió a dar sus 'Frutos'
articles.standfirst: El Rayo volvió a jugar los 90 minutos en Vallecas con su afición al completo
articles.summary: El Rayo volvió a jugar los 90 minutos en Vallecas con su afición al completo
articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano en su plenitud. Con todo su público y en su estadio, consiguió la victoria. El conjunto franjirrojo llevaba sin ganar en su sede desde la temporada pasada y lo consiguió ante el Euro Celta. El encuentro estuvo marcado por la vuelta de la grada de animación y por el doblete de Jorge De Frutos. El de Navares de Enmedio aún no se había estrenado en liga y estuvo brillante en las dos finalizaciones. No tenía una pareja de baile fácil. El sistema de Claudio Giráldez obligó a los extremos rivales a aplicarse tanto en defensa como en ataque. De Frutos tenía en frente a Javi Galán, pero el jugador rayista supo medir los tiempos y hacer daño cuando la jugada lo requirió. En el minuto 35 llegó su primer momento de gloria. Después de fallar un control en su banda derecha y que la grada le animara, se ayudó en Camello para trazar la jugada y anotar el primer gol del partido con la pierna izquierda. El siguiente tanto llegó en la segunda parte, en el 55'. Ratiu no le vio desmarcarse en el comienzo de la jugada y en una de sus rápidas internadas probó el remate que se estrelló contra un defensa. El rumano se aprovechó del rebote y mediante un 'sombrero' y varios amagos fue absorbiendo jugadores celestes para habilitar a De Frutos que 'machacó' la red. El último doblete de Jorge De Frutos fue el 4 de marzo ante el Real Oviedo en la jornada 23 de la temporada pasada. El Rayo Vallecano volvió a la senda de la victoria de la mejor forma posible. Tras el pitido final, los jugadores hicieron un corro dentro del campo y la voz cantante la llevó Beñat San José. Aplaudieron a la afición y esta les correspondió. Como siempre. Al final se acercaron a hablar con el fondo, pero no llegó a sonar la 'Vida Pirata'. Todavía no.

articles.title: Brighton shock Man City, closing gap on Premier League leader to two points
articles.summary: Yasin Ayari goal hands third-placed Brighton 1-0 win at Manchester City, with two points separating top three in EPL.
articles.body:
Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points of the leaders on Saturday.

Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first-ever away win against City on their 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title.

The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials.

Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday.

Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad and this time held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead.

Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time.

But the visitors were well worthy of a famous win and could also have added to their lead when Jack Hinshelwood hit the side netting late on.

City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola.

However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.

City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld, they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top flight.

Defeat for Maresca’s men means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday.

articles.title: Coventry win leaves Man United on brink of Premier League relegation zone
articles.summary: Manchester United one place outside the EPL’s bottom three as Coventry City climb with 3-1 win over Sunderland.
articles.body:
Joint record Premier League winners Manchester United were plunged to the brink of the relegation zone by their defeat at Chelsea followed by Coventry City’s win against Sunderland.

Ten-man United were beaten 2-0 at Stamford Bridge in the early kickoff in the English top flight, leaving them on their first nine-match winless run since 1986. The Red Devils have already made their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Despite an improved display in the first -half, in which recalled captain Bruno Fernandes spurned one of many key chances, United were beaten by a brilliant solo goal by Morgan Rogers and a penalty converted by Cole Palmer.

Lisandro Martinez was shown a second yellow card for a reckless challenge on Wesley Fofana in an aerial duel from a corner.

Coventry City’s 3-1 home win against Sunderland saw them leapfrog the fallen giants, leaving United just one point and one place outside the relegation zone.

There’s a chance the 20-time English champions, who have won only once in nine league games, could be in the bottom three by the end of Matchweek 9 – a desperate situation for a club widely regarded as the biggest in the country.

Man United’s only two victories from 13 matches in all competitions this season were against promoted Ipswich in the Premier League and tournament newcomer Sabah in the Champions League.

United’s next match is at home to Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday with yet more doubts on whether Carrick will still be in charge.

“I think the mentality was there right from the first minute,” United forward Bryan Mbeumo said. “We still trust everyone.

“Maybe today we just missed some chances. We could have been up early in the game, but that’s a positive to take out of this game.”

Only Nottingham Forest’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford ensured United did not drop into the bottom three.

The pressure is piling onto Carrick, who is only in his first full season in charge.

The former midfielder remains in defiant mood.

“The two halves of football couldn’t probably be further apart,” said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League tie against Roma.

“We looked in a good place going into half-time and then found a way of unravelling it second half.”

A point for Crystal Palace in the final Premier League game of the day at Tottenham will see United fall into the bottom three.

articles.title: Pau Navarro se disculpa por la polémica generada por sus palabras: "Me gustaría ver el estadio siempre lleno"
articles.standfirst: El defensa del Villarreal asegura que sus palabras tras la derrota ante el Espanyol no pretendían señalar a la afición
articles.summary: El defensa del Villarreal asegura que sus palabras tras la derrota ante el Espanyol no pretendían señalar a la afición
articles.body: Pau Navarro ha salido al paso de la polémica generada por sus declaraciones tras la derrota del Villarreal frente al Espanyol. El defensa amarillo publicó este sábado un mensaje en sus redes sociales para aclarar sus palabras y pedir disculpas a aquellos aficionados que se hayan sentido molestos por unas manifestaciones que provocaron un intenso debate entre el entorno 'groguet'. En una historia de Instagram, el futbolista quiso dejar claro que su reflexión no pretendía justificar el resultado ni desviar la atención de los problemas deportivos que atraviesa el equipo. "No fue ninguna excusa por haber perdido el partido, ni lo será en ningún otro", afirmó. En su comunicado, recordó que en la entrevista posterior al encuentro también analizó "las muchas cosas que no estamos haciendo bien y que tenemos que mejorar". Navarro insistió en que tanto él como el vestuario son conscientes de las dificultades del equipo y de la necesidad de elevar el rendimiento para revertir la situación. "Todos somos conscientes de que tenemos que corregir cosas y esforzarnos más para mejorar", señaló. El origen de la controversia se encuentra en unas declaraciones realizadas después del encuentro ante el Espanyol, cuando el canterano lamentó la escasa presencia de aficionados en los minutos finales del partido en La Cerámica. "No puede ser que en el minuto 75 el campo esté vacío. Tenemos que ir todos a una, eso marca la diferencia. Cuando vas a otros campos, los últimos minutos aprietan muchísimo y aquí tenemos que hacernos fuertes", dijo en declaraciones a Movistar. Sus palabras fueron interpretadas como una crítica al apoyo recibido desde la grada en un momento delicado para el conjunto castellonense. Ante esa reacción, el jugador ha querido matizar su mensaje y subrayar que hablaba desde su condición de aficionado del Villarreal. "Simplemente quise explicar, como aficionado del Villarreal que soy, que me gustaría ver el estadio siempre lleno porque vuestro apoyo es clave para nosotros", explicó. El futbolista defendió además la necesidad de reforzar la unión entre plantilla y afición para afrontar una etapa en la que los resultados no están respondiendo a las expectativas. "Ahora que las cosas no nos están saliendo como queremos, sois muy importantes y tenemos que estar unidos", añadió. El comunicado concluye con un mensaje de agradecimiento a los seguidores amarillos y una llamada a mirar hacia adelante de cara al próximo compromiso liguero, que el Villarreal disputará el martes en La Cerámica. "Equipo y afición tenemos que ir juntos y ser uno", reivindicó Navarro antes de despedirse.

articles.title: El Madrid recupera a Courtois y pierde a Valverde para medirse al Racing

articles.body: El Real Madrid ha ofrecido la lista de convocados para el partido de mañana en El Sardinero (16:15 horas) y la mala noticia para Mourinho es que Valverde no se ha recuperado de sus molestias después de salir tocado del triunfo en el Clásico. La buena noticia para Mou es que Courtois, que se perdió el partido ante el Barça por una gripe, regresa a la lista. El entrenador del Real Madrid ha confirmado esta tarde en la rueda de prensa que Valverde no iba a ser titular. Una vez que se ha quedado fuera de la lista, lo normal es que ocupe el lateral derecho Dumfries, ya que está contando con más minutos a las órdenes del luso que Trent aunque ninguno esté siendo titular. La duda es si Courtois será titular ante el Racing. Hasta el momento solo se ha perdido el encuentro ante el Barça por baja médica, pero Lunin se ganó los elogios de Mou tras el Clásico y ha admitido que no está pudiendo ser justo con él porque merece más minutos. De no hacerlo mañana, es probable que el ucraniano tenga algún partido, bien de Liga o de Copa. El que repite en la lista es Militao, ya recuperado. La intención del entrenador es que vaya sumando minutos hasta entrar en el once dado que lo considera un pilar en la defensa. Porteros: Courtois, Lunin y Mestre. articles.title: Le Bris confident he has backing as Sunderland’s struggles continue
articles.summary: Regis Le Bris admits Sunderland are in a relegation battle this season after their poor Premier League form continued with a 3-1 defeat to Coventry.The Sunde...
articles.body:
Regis Le Bris admits Sunderland are in a relegation battle this season after their poor Premier League form continued with a 3-1 defeat to Coventry.

The Sunderland boss insists the club were prepared for a difficult second season in the top flight. particularly with the extra demands of qualifying for Europe, and says his players must retain the "underdog mentality" that helped them establish themselves in the Premier League.

Asked directly whether Sunderland are now fighting relegation, Le Bris said: "It's obvious.

"If you look at the table, there's no doubt about the situation. I think Sunderland in the Premier League for the second year has to have this mindset, the underdog mentality.

"I repeat, the situation is not unexpected. We started the season with this understanding of how demanding it could be, and it's the case. So we are ready for that.

"Are we happy? I repeat, no. Are we worried? Always, because it's football. Elite football is like that. You can't relax at all.

"Are we combative? Yes. Are we resilient? Yes. Are we together? Yes. And we'll bounce back quickly."

Le Bris believes Sunderland's busy schedule has contributed to their struggles and pointed to the difficulties clubs can experience when competing in Europe for the first time.

"We are growing fast. We are exposed this season with this busy schedule and it's really demanding," he said.

"Is it unexpected? I don't think so. Many clubs last year experienced exactly the same situation.

"First year in Europe, you know that we'll have on average 10 less points. It's our reality.

"Does it mean that we are happy? Absolutely not. We have to get better because it's hard to play this first half. It's hard to not be able to play our football with confidence, with the ability to be ourselves."

Le Bris also dismissed concerns over whether he retains the backing of the club and his players.

"We experienced so many difficult situations to achieve what we achieved, and we won't give up just because it's a bit tough at the beginning of the season.

"So, 100% I'm combative. I feel the unity of the club.

"I don't feel that the players are trying to escape their own responsibilities, which is the most important, I think.

"For the staff, it's the case. For me, it's the case. So, I keep working hard."

articles.title: Brilliant Brighton show Carragher's chain must be broken when Man City charges case ends
articles.summary: Brighton have beaten the the two best teams in England this season and are two points off the top of the Premier League. Why should they accept their place i...
articles.body:
ETIHAD STADIUM, MANCHESTER – A month has passed since Chargeageddon, as it almost certainly isn't known in these parts.

A month into the Manchester City siege mentality since the club were found guilty of the vast majority of charges of financial malpractice brought against them by the Premier League . City continue to protest their innocence and have launched an appeal.

A sanctions hearing must also take place and, if the most serious breaches relating to disguised funding schemes are upheld, City face historically severe punishments.

In the dugout, Enzo Maresca and his exciting young side must continue with the business of a title race. They headed into this weekend top of the shop despite a defeat at Aston Villa last time out in the Premier League, thanks to seven wins from eight. City's 11th English league championship will be the aim until the arbitration process tells them otherwise.

In the other corner were Brighton and Hove Albion, third in the table, having already hammered champions Arsenal this season. A defeat at Anfield last weekend marked a blip in their progress, but Saturday's hard-fought 1-0 win over Manchester City can extinguish any lingering doubts that Fabian Hurzeler's side are the real deal.

Albion drew 2-2 on this ground before losing a Carabao Cup tie on penalties in midweek. Fabian Hurtzeler made six changes to that XI and, after 12 minutes, Brighton led at the Etihad Stadium for the third time in four days. City right-back Matheus Nunes missed a clearance and the ball bounced fortuitously off Maxim De Cuyper for Yasin Ayari to make amends for his Wednesday night failure in the shootout.

City had offered nothing to speak of at that point and threatened fleetingly for the rest of a nip-and-tuck first half. Iliman Ndiaye should have headed home after the ever-impressive Elliot Anderson delivered a sumptuous cross, and the visitors also had a penalty appeal for handball against Lewis Dunk – Brighton's other spot-kick culprit in midweek – waved away during stoppage time.

The game opened up as anticipated after the break. De Cuyper never got over a bouncing ball from Ayari and should have done better at the back post. Both goalkeepers then made fine saves – Bart Verbruggen turning an Ndiaye piledriver against his left post before Gianluigi Donnarumma scrambled to claw De Cuyper's header to safety.

City finally built a head of steam by the hour, with playmaker Rayan Cherki's introduction not coincidental to this. Brighton needed heroics from Verbruggen to thwart Nunes. Then there was then the rarely seen spectacle of Hurzeler's side really having to dig in. Customarily, they take the sting out of periods of pressure so well. Out of possession, they are positionally outstanding. This is a platform for well-directed tenacity and means they are always in a position to turn defence into attack.

Aided by a couple of poor misses from Ndiaye and substitute Nico O'Reilly, the Seagulls became the first team to prevent City from scoring in any competition this season. They celebrated with gusto at full-time, the travelling supporters exploding as if the final whistle was a second goal

At odds with their coach's demeanour – Hurzeler is a gurning windmill of perma-rage in the technical area – Brighton are cold and calculating in the way properly good teams are. This has been an impressive aspect of this side's evolution. They can put the hammer down with the best of them, but this is not simply the pressing and threshing machine set in motion by Roberto De Zerbi and taken on by Hurzeler. Diego Gomez and the evergreen Pascal Gross give them a few more gears.

This result means Brighton are two points behind City and Arsenal ahead of the champions' visit to Liverpool on Sunday. This year marked the 10th anniversary of Leicester City 's title heist, so why not? The thing is, the Premier League is designed for things like that not to happen.

The past couple of days have brought another of those events that leads you to marvel at our terminally online contemporary timeline. On one of the biggest podcast platforms in soccer, Jamie Carragher told Aston Villa fans to "f— off", Villa's owner spuriouly threatened legal action and the former Liverpool defender then posted a fawning apology on social media.

Carragher saying a rude word shouldn't really cause anyone to lose sleep, never mind instruct lawyers. The comments came in the midst of a discussion over whether Manchester United should approach Aston Villa to appoint their manager Unai Emery.

Emery won the Europa League with Villa last season, oversaw a hasty squad rebuild during the summer, beat City last weekend and has the Birmingham club riding high again. Why on earth would he join a Manchester United who, after taking seven points from their first nine games, we can refer to as relegation-threatened with a straightish face?

"There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not," Carragher opined. The obvious response is, well, why would you like that unless it benefits your club?

Brighton are frequently referred to as the best-run club in the Premier League. This was their third season without defeat at the Etihad Stadium. They've also won each of their past two home matches against City, the most accomplished English team of the past decade, irrespective of how their successes were achieved and what sanctions might be in the post.

But no one really considers the idea that a Brighton squad packed with talent might win the league this season. Maybe they'll finish in the Champions League places, continuing a dizzying rise for the Tony Bloom-owned club.

At that point, the brilliant Luka Vuskovic – who so brilliantly shackled Erling Haaland here – probably becomes a solution for United or Liverpool's centre-back woes. Just like Carlos Baleba was for United's midfield refit this summer. Chelsea would probably return as frequent shoppers on England's south coast. They pipped Liverpool to Moises Caicedo's signature in 2023. The Reds had to make do with Alexis Mac Allister.

That's Carragher's chain in action, and Brighton play their position in it perfectly. But the rewards for such clubs should be greater, when the richest can oversee repeated waste and failure in the transfer market before plucking their next gem from Brighton, Brentford or Bournemouth to fix the mess.

Like it or not? Honestly, what's to like. If City's appeal is unsuccessful and the verdict remains that the only team to break into English football's modern elite and stay there did so because they cheated to the tune of £900m over a nine-year period, it will be time for a proper conversation about how we organise the richest domestic club competition in world soccer more equitably.

Spending being anchored to the income of the lowest-earning club was one proposal floated in recent years. The Premier League could examine spending caps for transfers and/or wages that are not linked primarily to turnover. There could be hard limits on squad size and a stipulation to fill spots with players from academies that turn too many young men into mere balance sheet commodities under the current system of financial regulation.

Do these things or do something. Break the chain. Because crocodile tears over how City have harmed clubs like Brighton are just that if the status quo that exploits those from outside the elite remains.

articles.title: Peter Schmeichel fires accusation against “absolute disgrace” Lisandro Martinez after Chelsea nightmare
articles.summary: Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel ripped Lisandro Martinez apart following his horror show in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.AbysmalTwo w...
articles.body:
Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel ripped Lisandro Martinez apart following his horror show in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

Two weeks after he controversially called out the United hierarchy for lacking ambition and failing during the summer window, Martinez endured another tough game as United were beaten by Chelsea.

The Argentina international gave away a reckless penalty and was consequently sent off after picking up two yellow cards in quick succession.

His performance was already of a poor standard when he received a booking in the 60th minute for pulling back Morgan Rogers. Shortly afterwards, he elbowed Wesley Fofana in the face while United were defending a corner.

Replays revealed he never looked at the ball, his focus entirely on Fofana, while Michael Carrick completely ignored Martinez as he headed down the tunnel.

A man down and trailing by two, United faced an impossible comeback task as their winless run stretched to nine matches.

Speaking after the final whistle, Schmeichel was hugely critical of Martinez, squarely blaming him for United's loss. The Dane also accused Martinez of trying to orchestrate an exit.

The iconic United goalkeeper said [as quoted by SportBible ], "I put this solely on Lisandro Martinez's shoulders. This is an absolute disgrace how he played this game."

"Two weeks ago, he came out and made some very, very strong statements against his teammates, against the football club, and it felt like he was trying to orchestrate a move."

"He's in the last year of his contract. What he did today, honestly, I have no words."

"The first goal, I mean, he's played a World Cup final. Somebody who's played a World Cup final can't defend the way he defended on the first goal."

"The penalty… I have no words. I literally have no words for how crazy that was. And then he walks off the pitch, shaking his head as if he's done nothing wrong. So bad."

United are next in action on Tuesday when they face AS Roma in the Champions League.
